claims.text: Untreated single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a derivative has a room-temperature coercive field of approximately 100 Oe.
Plasma nitriding can incorporate a small, uniform interstitial nitrogen concentration into FeCoNi.
Plasma nitriding at approximately 400–500 °C can avoid secondary-phase formation in FeCoNi.
Interstitial nitrogen will induce tetragonal lattice distortion in the FeCoNi matrix.
The nitrogen-treated matrix will remain predominantly fcc.
Nitrogen-induced lattice distortion will increase magnetic anisotropy.
Increased magnetic anisotropy will enhance domain-wall pinning during magnetization reversal.
Enhanced domain-wall pinning will increase the coercive field.
The nitrided material will have a coercive field significantly above 100 Oe.
The nitrided material may exhibit a coercivity increase of at least 50% relative to the untreated control.
The nitrided material will largely retain the high saturation magnetization of the untreated material.
The coercivity increase may depend on the degree of nitrogen incorporation.
The coercivity increase may depend on the uniformity of nitrogen incorporation and local microstructural inhomogeneities.

contradictions.description: The initial state and baseline allow an unspecified high-entropy-alloy derivative, whereas the boundary restricts the experiment to near-stoichiometric FeCoNi without other alloying additions, leaving the derivative option incompatible with or excluded by the stated boundary.
